name: GMM Pfaudler Ltd
title: GMM Pfaudler Ltd - 505255 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Order intake up 20% to INR 3,714 crore and opening backlog up 34%, but management declined numeric FY27 guidance, Q4 gross margin slipped and EBITDA margin target is only 15% medium term.

summary.headline: GMM Pfaudler FY26 revenue rose about 10% and EBITDA about 11% to INR 403 crore; Q4 gross margin fell, with no FY27 numeric guidance.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue grew about 10% and EBITDA rose from INR 361 crore to INR 403 crore, with full-year margin up about 1 percentage point. India was the standout, with revenue up about 12%, EBITDA up about 24% and PAT up about 40%. Q4 margins fell year-on-year and sequentially on a large HE (heavy engineering) shipment and higher gas and metal costs, which management called quarter-specific. FY26 order intake reached INR 3,714 crore (up about 20% from INR 3,100 crore) and opening backlog on April 1 was up about 34%. Management declined to give numeric FY27 guidance and said it would present a three-year plan to the market later.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 12%, EBITDA about 24% and PAT about 40% in FY26. Heavy engineering (Ahmedabad) did about INR 300+ crore revenue in FY26, and the Vatva facility (GMM Inox, Poland) grew double digits.

segments.name: Europe / International
segments.commentary: Execution was slow; international EBITDA margin cited at about 10%. German restructuring is expected to save INR 45 crore a year once fully absorbed. Europe order intake was much stronger in FY26, including large systems orders.

segments.name: Mixing / Edlon / SEMCO
segments.commentary: Edlon (semiconductor-linked high-purity linings) is now about USD 25 million revenue, which management called high margin. SEMCO (South America) won a USD 12-13 million agitator order in Q1 FY27; MixPro (Canada) is growing and profitable.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 guidance; management said it expects improvement in FY27 on a 12-month basis, citing order intake, backlog and restructuring.
Medium-term EBITDA margin aspiration of at least 15% at consolidated level, versus about 11.4-11.5% today.
Three-year strategy (growth, cost, organisation) prepared; market presentation targeted for August-September, possibly later given Middle East crisis.
Expects no significant one-off restructuring cost in FY27; the INR 45 crore German saving starts next year and fully materialises as staff retire.
Plans to repay about USD 20 million from group cash and reduce debt, but timing of the financing restructuring is not confirmed by end of FY27.
Target of at least double-digit revenue growth over about three years, but management said 20% growth in a year is unlikely to be planned for.
capex_capacity: GMM Inox (Poland, 51% owned, strong local partner) is full; two more sheds are needed as soon as possible to serve European sites with lower cost.
Vatva facility (GMM Inox) could reach about INR 700-800 crore revenue with small further investment; beyond that a new facility is needed.
UK and Hyderabad facilities shut; German factory downsized; Poland plant now operating.
Edlon and SEMCO acquisitions added intangibles and goodwill; split not given on call, to be shared offline.
demand_pricing: Order intake up about 20% to INR 3,714 crore; nearly 50% from non-traditional industries (semiconductors, defence, oil and gas, petrochemicals, metals and minerals, nuclear).
Two large systems orders (one US, one Eastern Europe) drove much of the increase; open systems opportunities could yield USD 20-30 million order intake per year.
Chemicals (especially agrochemicals and European chemicals) remain slow; pharma (CDMO, GLP drugs) improving; China business recovering in some segments.
Raw material pass-through depends on contract: long-term projects have a 5% expedition clause; fast-moving contracts absorb cost changes.
Q1 FY27 order intake continuing at a decent level, including an Edlon order of USD 8-9 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross and consolidated EBITDA margins (55.4% gross) drop, and what are sustainable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 to a large HE order shipped at lower margin and higher gas and metal costs that have since stabilised. It said quarterly margins are volatile and FY26 margin was up about 1 pp; it prefers 12-month views.

qa_highlights.question: Why no guidance for FY27, and what drives the growth and margin plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20% order-intake rise includes systems orders that convert over 2-3 years, so it avoided a bullish number. It plans a three-year strategy to be presented to the capital markets once confidence improves, targeting at least double-digit growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the German restructuring saving and will exceptional items recur?
qa_highlights.answer: The German restructuring saves INR 45 crore a year, starting next year. No significant one-off cost is planned for FY27, though future restructurings would be reported as one-offs. FY26 exceptional items were about INR 65 crore, including German severance and the India labour code impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the finance cost high relative to a small net debt, and how does the company plan to reduce it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited FX on an intercompany loan between Germany and Luxembourg, and a financing agreement in place until 2028, which it intends to restructure within the next year. It said the high cash balance is partly customer prepayments needed to finance large systems orders.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term margin targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to a 15% consolidated EBITDA margin in the medium term, as a minimum, versus about 11.4-11.5% today, and said it could come faster if initiatives work.

qa_highlights.question: Will the segment reporting change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reporting format will change from next quarter (Q1 FY27), with a new organisation aligned by product, vertical and industry, rather than mid-year.

risks_watch: Gross margin and mix volatility: Q4 margins fell and management said it is quarter-specific; watch whether FY27 margins recover.
Tax rate: international tax remains high, mainly from the Luxembourg entity and an intercompany FX loan; Q4 international rate was about 30%.
Finance cost of about INR 120-130 crore against low net debt; restructuring timeline is uncertain and may slip beyond FY27.
Middle East conflict and geopolitical tension could delay investments in Europe and Asia; management said it may delay its capital markets presentation.
Chemicals demand remains weak; systems orders are lumpy and convert to revenue over 2-3 years.
Changed segment reporting expected from Q1 FY27; SEMCO purchase price allocation split was not disclosed on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident about order intake and India performance, but deliberately cautious on FY27 numbers, citing the Middle East crisis and macro uncertainty. Management was defensive on Q4 margins and on the financing structure and tax, and repeatedly deferred timelines.
key_quotes: We would like to at least maintain or grow margins in the next year.
So, we are confident, but we also do not want to be too bullish.
The last thing we want is to come out and give a number and then not achieve it.
We will repay or intend to repay easily 20 million USD…

Vatva facility (GMM Inox) could reach INR 700-800 crore revenue with small further investment; beyond that a new facility needed

growth.why: No numeric FY27 guidance; management expects FY27 improvement on a 12-month basis backed by FY26 order intake up ~20% to INR 3,714 crore, opening backlog up ~34%, and the INR 45 crore German restructuring saving, plus a medium-term target of at least double-digit revenue growth over about three years and a 15%+ EBITDA margin aspiration.
